title: BUG: Forces were zeroed in NEB trajectories for constrained atoms.
body:
This is a minimal fix for an issue that trajectories created by `NEB` were saving *constrained*, not raw, forces. (That is, `calc.results` was full of a lot of zeroes when fixed atoms were present, like in the [NEB dissociation tutorial](https://ase-lib.org/examples_generated/tutorials/neb_dissociation.html).)

Note this is part of a larger issue with how `NEB` passes info to the trajectory writer: it ends up only saving energy and forces, and nothing else (so the rest of `calc.results` and all of `calc.parameters` is discarded). It appears this was done for the special case of parallel-calculator NEBs, but ended up affecting all NEBs. But that's a bigger fix, and a broader discussion (tied to my very-old but still-very-much-desired MR !2395 -- just updated!).

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Thank you @andrew_peterson for finding this issue! I agree this is a bug to be fixed, and the MR addresses this, considering also parallelization. I just updated a changelog statement on my side because this is an issue for general constraints as well, where forces are not necessarily zero but anyway different from the unconstraint ones. I also added a test to check the unconstrained forces are different from the constrained ones. I run the pipeline on the main ASE repo now (https://gitlab.com/ase/ase/-/pipelines/2406167708); once this is passed, I would like to merge soon.
